title: uxaudit project context
description: Schema for the Scout-produced project-context.json file. This captures the product's declared purpose, discovered journeys, and lightweight experience model so downstream evaluation can stay project-shaped without exposing the full spec to Judges.

confidence.description: How much trust this journey hypothesis can carry. `high` = the journey is backed by something the team actively maintains (e.g., an e2e test running in CI, a recent scenario doc the team references). `medium` = synthesized from routes or README structure — declared intent, but not actively validated. `low` = adapted from a category baseline or derived from JTBD inference. The downstream pipeline weights fails by this value: a fail on a low-confidence journey is information about the hypothesis as much as about the product. Optional but strongly recommended — when absent, the downstream treats the journey as `medium`.

first_value_signals.description: Concrete observable indicators that the journey's first_value (declared on the linked job in experience_model.jobs) was actually delivered. The L4 Judge uses these signals to evaluate the `value_delivery` axis of journey_evaluation: it operates the journey, then checks the final state for these specific signals. Example for a recipe app's 'find a recipe' journey: ['Recipe detail page rendered with ingredients list', 'Cook time visible at the top of the page', 'No empty-state placeholder where recipe content should be']. Optional — when absent, the Judge falls back to interpreting the job-level first_value string directly.

intentional_friction.description: Steps the design team purposely added that LOOK like excise but are actually required friction (Cooper's idiom-required friction): irreversibility guards, shoulder-surf guards, payment confirmations, trust-building steps. The L4 Judge uses this list to evaluate the `operating_cost` axis: it counts actual_steps, matches each against `matches` semantically, and classifies the unmatched excess as unintentional excise. Without this list, every step beyond the minimum looks like a fail; with it, the Judge can correctly say 'this 11-step journey is fine because 3 of the steps are declared trust-building moments'.

matches.description: Plain-language description of the step the Judge should match against. Natural language because the Judge does semantic matching against what it observes — e.g., 'type DELETE to confirm' will match a confirmation modal regardless of the exact button label or flow position. Step numbers are deliberately NOT used because they shift between iterations.

rationale.description: Why this friction is justified. e.g., 'Account deletion is irreversible — prevent accidental click' or 'Re-enter password before payment to prevent unauthorized transactions on an unattended device'. Becomes the `rationale` field in the Judge's excise_attribution output when this entry matches a step.

audit_policy.description: Tells the Journey Compiler which categories of side-effectful actions it is allowed to actually exercise. Defaults: allow_llm_spend=true, allow_payment=false, allow_destructive_delete=false. The Compiler reads this block before translating any click that spends money, creates irreversible state, or calls a paid LLM API. See agents/uxaudit-journey-compiler.md § audit_policy.

allow_llm_spend.description: When true (the default), the Compiler clicks Generate/Submit on LLM-API-spending steps normally. When false, the Compiler fills the form and records the step in non_fakeable_skips.

allow_payment.description: When true, the Compiler clicks through real-money checkout. Default is false — only set true when the project uses a test-mode payment provider (Stripe test keys, PayPal sandbox).

allow_destructive_delete.description: When true, the Compiler clicks Delete Account / Drop Table / Revoke Key. Default is false — only set true when the project has a reliable reset mechanism between runs.

rate_limit_tokens.description: Soft cap on total LLM tokens spent across all journeys in a single audit run.

notes.description: Short explanation of any non-default value.
